item.title: A benchmark is not your corpus
item.description: I run a second brain. Not a metaphor, a folder: ~6,500 curated notes, 24,226 chunks, half Russian, half English. Decisions, post-mortems, other people's lessons, my own screw-ups. When I ask it something, it searches by meaning, not by words.

item.title: September 10, 2026: Memory, Boundaries, and the Cost of Automation
item.description: The day's posts looked scattered: lead scoring, message cleanup, AI-agent memory, subscription economics, job applications, TRIZ, and even conference hygiene. Underneath them was one shared question: how do you make an automated system useful without letting it become careless, opaque, or expensive?

item.title: September 9, 2026: Bodies, Digital Selves, and Narrow AI That Actually Helps
item.description: Today's posts looked at the same problem from two different distances: what makes a person persist, and what part of that persistence can be built with today's tools.
